summary: Extends the Opus audio codec to store coded Ambisonics, a surround-sound format, in the Ogg container. It also updates RFC 7845 for changes in the description of channel mapping families.

eli5.summary: Some sound recordings catch noises from all around you. This explains how to save them in an Opus file.

subtitle: Two new channel mapping families that let Ogg Opus files carry surround-sound Ambisonics.

tldr.problem: Ogg Opus had no way to say that a multichannel stream holds Ambisonics, a representation of three-dimensional sound fields used for surround sound and immersive virtual reality.
tldr.mechanism: It defines channel mapping family 2 (Ambisonic channels sent individually) and family 3 (channels recovered by multiplying decoded channels by a demixing matrix). It also reserves families 240 through 254 for experiments and updates RFC 7845.
tldr.outcome: Players can now recognize Ambisonics in Ogg Opus, downmix it to stereo or mono, and treat unknown families safely. It is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 8486 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 7845, and the metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Ambisonics is a representation format for three-dimensional sound fields that can be used for surround sound and immersive virtual-reality playback. For this document it can be treated as a multichannel audio stream. A separate stereo stream can play alongside it in a head-tracked VR experience as non-diegetic audio, meaning audio that does not change when the listener turns their head, such as narration or stereo music.

Ogg is a general-purpose container that can carry audio coded with the Opus codec (see RFC 6716 and RFC 7845). This RFC extends Ogg Opus by adding two new channel mapping families, with values 2 and 3, to the IANA "Opus Channel Mapping Families" registry. The mapping can also be used in other contexts that use that registry. It also reserves families 240 through 254 for experimental use.
sections.eli5: Imagine a recording that remembers where every sound came from, up, down, left or right. This RFC teaches an audio file format how to label such a recording.

sections.title: Channel Mapping Family 2
sections.content:
An Ogg Opus stream selects Ambisonics by setting the channel mapping family to 2 or 3 in the Ogg identification header. A demuxer that sees 2 or 3 MUST interpret the stream as Ambisonics in the format described for that family.

Family 2 uses the same channel mapping table format as family 1. The output channels are Ambisonic components in Ambisonic Channel Number (ACN) order, followed by two optional channels of non-diegetic stereo (left, right). ACN is defined as ACN = n * (n + 1) + m for order n and degree m. For a channel at index k, the order is n = floor(sqrt(k)) and the degree is m = k - n * (n + 1).

Family 2 allows mixed-order Ambisonics, where only a subset of the channels of a full order is encoded. The channel count field gives the full number, and the inactive ACNs are marked in the channel mapping field with the index 255. Channels use Schmidt Semi-Normalization (SN3D), as described in the ambiX paper.
sections.eli5: Family 2 is like a numbered row of seats. Each seat holds one direction of sound in a fixed order, and a seat can be marked empty with 255.

sections.title: Channel Mapping Family 3 and the Demixing Matrix
sections.content:
In family 3, C output channels are produced at the decoder by multiplying K = N + M decoded channels by a demixing matrix D with C rows and K columns. Here N is the number of streams encoded and M is how many of them are coupled to produce two channels. C and K do not have to be equal. The output is S = D X, where X holds the K decoded channels. Like family 2, it supports full-order and mixed-order Ambisonics and non-diegetic stereo, with the added flexibility of mixing channels.

The matrix MUST be given in the channel mapping table of the identification header, and it replaces the channel mapping field. The table holds:

  • Stream Count (8 bits, unsigned): the total number of streams in each Ogg packet.
  • Coupled Stream Count (8 bits, unsigned): how many of those streams are decoded to two channels (stereo).
  • Demixing Matrix (16*K*C bits, signed): coefficients stored in column-major order as 16-bit signed two's complement fixed-point values with 15 fractional bits (Q15), little endian.

The output gain field can be used for a normalization scale. In mixed-order representations, silent ACN channels are shown by all zeros in the matching rows. The total output channel count C MUST be set in the third field of the identification header.

RFC 7845 says the identification header cannot exceed one page, which is 65,025 octets. With full order and a coded stream count equal to the Ambisonic order plus the two non-diegetic channels, this means the order MUST be lower than 12.
sections.eli5: Family 3 sends a recipe instead of a seating chart. The recipe is a grid of numbers telling the player how to blend the coded sounds into each final channel.

sections.title: Allowed Numbers of Channels
sections.content:
For both families, the allowed channel counts are (1 + n)^2 + 2j for n = 0, 1, ..., 14 and j = 0 or 1. Here n is the highest Ambisonic order and j says whether a separate non-diegetic stereo stream is present. That covers periphonic Ambisonics from zeroth to fourteenth order, plus optionally two stereo channels.

The explicit list is 1, 3, 4, 6, 9, 11, 16, 18, 25, 27, 36, 38, 49, 51, 64, 66, 81, 83, 100, 102, 121, 123, 144, 146, 169, 171, 196, 198, 225 and 227. The header length limit still applies: full order with that many coded streams must stay below order 12.
sections.eli5: Only certain numbers of tracks make sense, like square numbers (1, 4, 9, 16...), with two extra tracks allowed for a plain stereo voice-over.

sections.title: Downmixing to Stereo and Mono
sections.content:
The downmix matrices are only examples known to give acceptable stereo results, and other mixing strategies are allowed, for example to emphasize a certain panning. Omitted coefficients are 0.0.

With no non-diegetic stereo, a player MAY use a matrix where L takes 0.5 of W and 0.5 of Y, and R takes 0.5 of W and -0.5 of Y. W and Y are the first and second Ambisonic channels. With a non-diegetic stereo track present, a player MAY use 0.25 and 0.25 for L and 0.25 and -0.25 for R on W and Y, plus 0.5 of Ls into L and 0.5 of Rs into R.

The first channel, W, is a mono stream of the average audio signal over all directions. Because it has no direction, players MAY use W directly for mono playback.
sections.eli5: If you only have two speakers, you can blend the all-around sound down to left and right. If you have one speaker, the first track already works as an all-around mix.

sections.title: Updates to RFC 7845
sections.content:
This RFC updates RFC 7845 in three ways.

  • Table format. RFC 7845 implied one fixed channel mapping table format for all families. It now says the format depends on the family, and that the RECOMMENDED format for new families is the one in its Figure 3 unless a family needs a custom one. Families 1 and 255 do not change; their text is adjusted to say their mapping follows that figure.
  • Unknown families. RFC 7845 said a demuxer meeting a reserved family value SHOULD act as though it is 255. Now a demuxer meeting a family it does not recognize SHOULD NOT try to decode the packets and SHOULD NOT use anything except the first 19 octets of the ID header packet and the comment header.
  • Experiments. Families 240 through 254 are reserved for experiments and in-development families, not only for Ambisonics. Implementers SHOULD use numbers not recently used and SHOULD advertise them. The Ambisonics experiments behind this RFC used 254 for family 2 and 253 for family 3.
sections.eli5: The older rulebook said to guess when meeting a strange label. The new rule is to stay out of it and not play something you do not understand. Some labels are set aside as scratch paper for trying new ideas.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
Implementations must follow the Ogg security considerations in Section 8 of RFC 7845. Because this extension gives meaning to more channels than the existing format requires, more allocations are needed, so care should be taken in any new allocation paths. Implementations MUST NOT overrun their allocated memory nor read from uninitialized memory when managing the Ambisonic channel mapping.

IANA added 17 new assignments to the "Opus Channel Mapping Families" registry. The table lists 0 (mono, L/R stereo), 1 (1-8 channel surround), 2 (Ambisonics as individual channels), 3 (Ambisonics with demixing matrix), 240-254 (experimental use) and 255 (discrete channels).
sections.eli5: More tracks mean more memory to manage, so programs must be careful not to scribble outside their own space.
